situation: A product lead wanted to ship a major change on a Friday without rehearsing the rollback, to keep a date promised to customers.
decision: Ship Friday at 5% behind a flag and ramp the following Tuesday.

moves.name: who carries the cost if it fails
moves.step: For a risky launch, trace who absorbs the failure and when it lands.
moves.cue: a launch scheduled before a weekend
moves.evidence: those hours land on whoever is on call over the weekend, and the carriers ... absorb the failed routes

moves.name: price the risk and offer a cheaper path
moves.step: Instead of refusing, state the cost of the risky plan and offer lower-cost alternatives that keep the goal.
moves.cue: pressure to skip a safeguard to hold a date
moves.evidence: let me put a price on it instead of just saying no

moves.name: offer a smaller version that keeps the date
moves.step: Shrink the change (percentage, scope) so the promise is kept at lower risk.
moves.evidence: ship Friday at 5% of traffic behind the flag

moves.name: make the rollback the tested part
moves.step: Rehearse the undo path before relying on it; treat an untested rollback as the real risk.
moves.evidence: the rollback is the untested part - that is where the hours go

considerations.evidence: whoever is on call over the weekend
Either keeps the promise to the carriers
